title: /deployments/health/read discloses the effective probe interval and the browser decoder preserves it
description:
SPIDR child of task-078232fb9b9d4c06a5faf3c02adaf705, cut by architect-5ac70ba8 on 2026-09-07. THIS ROW TAKES the parent's DoD 4 verbatim; the parent keeps DoD 1's durable record, DoD 2 and DoD 3. dependsOn the parent because there is no effective interval to disclose until the parent lands the record and the default.

MEASURED AT HEAD by architect-5ac70ba8 (2026-09-07 ~13:20Z), and it settles the parent DoD 4's own conditional:
- The parent's DoD 4 said "once task-509c6c16 lands, else the current read". task-509c6c16 IS DONE ("HTTP /deployments/health/read serves environment state, the last error line and the open incident, composed into the production listener"). So this row binds to `/deployments/health/read`, not to a fallback.
- The browser client already exists: `apps/control-room/src/live/live-deployments-health.ts:21` exports `DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_READ_PATH = "/deployments/health/read"`, pinned at `live-deployments-health.test.ts:150` and rostered in `dev-proxy-paths.ts:28` and `live-document-proxy.test.ts:26`.

THE DECODER IS STRICTLY EXACT - READ THIS BEFORE DESIGNING THE WIRE. The control-room live decoders use an `exactDataRecord(value, expectedKeys)` helper that refuses when `keys.length !== expectedKeys.length`. There is NO optional-key path, so a new member must be emitted on EVERY row, always. Encode "unset" as an in-band value (the effective interval is always a number - the stored one or the 60000 default), never by omitting the key: an omitted key fails the length check and the WHOLE row decodes to null, blanking the screen rather than degrading one field. See Serena memory `decision-a-strictly-exact-wire-decoder-forces-an-always-emitted-key` for the full rule and the fixture-census recipe.

NOT IN SCOPE: the durable record, the store port, the scheduler and boot re-registration (the parent's), and the operator command kind (the sibling row filed alongside this one).
definitionOfDone: `/deployments/health/read` serves the EFFECTIVE probe interval per environment - the stored value when set, the 60000 default when unset - read through the port task-078232fb lands, never recomputed in the read.

The value is asserted against what was WRITTEN through the port and read back, never against a fixture constant the test also seeded - a self-agreeing assertion passes even when the read ignores the record.

The browser decoder in `apps/control-room/src/live/live-deployments-health.ts` preserves the member with EXACT-KEY decoding: an unknown key and a missing key each refuse with the specific code AND the layer that refused, and a malformed value fails closed rather than dropping the member silently.
Two environments with DIFFERENT stored intervals are disclosed separately and asserted by value - a read that serves one environment's interval for another passes every single-environment fixture.

Every fixture constructing the health view is backfilled for the new required member (census the literals, do not rely on the type name alone - a type-only import does not break). Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`.

THE DAEMON SERVES THE EFFECTIVE INTERVAL (DoD 1). In `apps/daemon/src/http/deployments-health-read.ts`:

1. Add the member to `DeploymentsHealthSource` (was :83-87, `{deploys, incidents, probes}`) — this is the seam that makes "read through the port" structurally true. The PORT supplies it; the read does not compute it.
2. Add the matching member to `DeploymentsHealthView` (was :62-76) and pass it straight through. No defaulting, no `??`, no recomputation in the handler — the parent's port already resolved stored-or-default into a single effective number.
3. Name it the same on both sides of the wire so the browser needs no key mapping (unlike `ok` -> `status`, which the decoder does map).

TYPE IT AS A PLAIN REQUIRED `number`. It is always present: the parent resolves the stored value or the 60000 default. Do not make it nullable — that would re-open a distinction the parent closed and force every consumer to re-apply the default.

The file was 251 lines, already at the 250 target: keep this to the two interface members and one pass-through. If it approaches 400, split rather than compressing existing comments.

COMPOSE THE INTERVAL INTO THE PRODUCTION PORT. In `apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts`, find `const deploymentsHealth = (): DeploymentsHealthReadPort =>` BY NAME (its line has moved — the parent edits this same file), and have it call the parent's interval port for the environment it is reading, putting the effective value into the `DeploymentsHealthSource` it returns.

This is the ONLY place the two rows meet. Re-read the surrounding code the parent landed before editing: it now registers a schedule per environment, so an interval-resolving helper may already be in scope and should be reused rather than re-derived.

If the port refuses for an environment (the parent's out-of-range or unknown-environment refusals), do NOT swallow it into the default — a refusal is a fact the read already knows how to carry: `DeploymentsHealthView` has a `probeRefusal` member and the source carries `HealthProbeResult`. Follow whichever the parent's port returns, and assert that path in step 4 with code AND layer rather than letting a refusal silently render as 60000.

DAEMON TESTS in `apps/daemon/src/http/deployments-health-read.test.ts`.

(a) WRITTEN-THEN-READ-BACK (DoD 2): write an interval through the parent's port, then assert the read serves THAT value — obtained by reading the port back, never compared against a constant the test also seeded. A self-agreeing assertion passes even when the read ignores the record entirely; the sibling row task-da60dc4b found exactly this defect already shipped in `deploy-rollback.test.ts:38`.
(b) UNSET SERVES THE DEFAULT: an environment with no stored record serves the parent's exported default — assert against the imported constant, not a retyped 60000.
(c) TWO ENVIRONMENTS, DIFFERENT VALUES (DoD 4): write two different intervals, read both, assert each environment gets its OWN. A read that serves one environment's interval for another passes every single-environment fixture, which is why this is its own arm.
(d) A PORT REFUSAL IS NOT LAUNDERED INTO THE DEFAULT: if the interval port refuses, assert the refusal surfaces with its code AND layer rather than the read quietly serving 60000.

DRILL (a) and (c): make the read return a hard-coded default and confirm (a) reds; make it resolve one environment's interval for all and confirm (c) reds. Restore each and prove with `git diff` (tracked paths).

THE BROWSER DECODER (DoD 3). In `apps/control-room/src/live/live-deployments-health.ts`, three small edits — the file was 216 lines, so there is room, but keep it tight.

1. `EnvironmentHealthView` (was :51-60): add the member as a required `number`, same name as the wire.
2. The exact-key roster (was :170, `["environment", "incident", "lastError", "lastProbe", "ok", "probeRefusal", "rollbackSha", "state"]`): add the key in alphabetical position. This is a KEY ROSTER change — 8 keys becoming 9.
3. The decode: require a real integer. A number check alone admits NaN, Infinity and non-integers; demand `Number.isInteger` and a positive value, and refuse otherwise with the existing `DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_RESPONSE_INVALID` @ `CONTROL_ROOM_DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH` (:16-18). Introduce no new code and no new layer constant.

A missing or unknown key already refuses through `exactDataRecord`'s length-and-membership check (:85-86) — do not add a second guard for it, and do not make the member optional: there is no optional-key path in that helper, and an omitted key collapses the whole environment row to null.

BROWSER TESTS AND THE FIXTURE BACKFILL.

In `apps/control-room/src/live/live-deployments-health.test.ts`:

(b) TWO environments with different intervals both survive, asserted by value — mirrors DoD 4 on the browser side.
(c) MALFORMED FAILS CLOSED (DoD 3): a string, a negative number, `1.5`, `NaN` and `null` each refuse `DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_RESPONSE_INVALID` @ `CONTROL_ROOM_DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH` — never a decoded row with the member dropped.
(d) MISSING KEY and UNKNOWN EXTRA KEY each refuse with the same code AND layer. Assert the WHOLE row fails to decode here, and say why in a comment: that is the omitted-key failure mode, and it is the reason the daemon always emits the key.
(e) BIDIRECTIONAL ROSTER (global rail): the new key is accepted AND an extra unknown key still refuses — a one-directional arm goes vacuous the next time the roster changes.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
REJECTED — computing the effective interval inside the read handler from the scheduler or the record directly. DoD 1 says "read through the port … never recomputed in the read", and a second resolution site is a second place for the stored-vs-default rule to drift. It enters through `DeploymentsHealthSource`, supplied by composition.

REJECTED — making the member nullable (`number | null`, null meaning unset). The parent already resolves stored-or-default into a single effective number, so a nullable wire member would re-open a distinction the parent closed and force every consumer to re-apply the default. One number, always present.

REJECTED — an optional key on the wire so the existing fixtures need no backfill. `exactDataRecord` (:77-90) has no optional-key path: an omitted key fails the length check and the whole environment row decodes to null, blanking the screen. Two backfill lines are cheaper than that failure mode, and the census shows only two files need them.

REJECTED — exporting the 60000 default from this row for the read to apply. The parent owns the default and exports it; re-declaring it here would be a second source of truth for the same fact. Import it, or better, never see it — the port hands over an already-effective number.

REJECTED — asserting the disclosed value against a fixture constant the test also seeded. DoD 2 forbids it explicitly, and the sibling row task-da60dc4b found exactly that defect already shipped in `deploy-rollback.test.ts:38`. Write through the port, read back through the port, compare.
